items.title: Variability of lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction between admission, discharge, and follow-up.
items.abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Using Lp(a) concentrations measured during stable follow-up as the reference, we aimed to assess the temporal variability of Lp(a) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to explore a pragmatic strategy for Lp(a) measurement. The FRENCHIE-Lp(a) cohort enrolled consecutive adults hospitalized for AMI in 21 centres. Lp(a) mass concentration, measured at admission, hospital discharge, and 3-12 months follow-up, was analysed both as a continuous and predefined categorical variable (≤20, >20-≤50, >50-≤70, >70 mg/dL). Assuming follow-up Lp(a) as the reference, we aimed to identify the threshold values that would allow us to accurately identify patients with Lp(a) > 70mg/dL, the threshold mostly used for patient selection in phase III trials of targeted Lp(a) therapies. A cumulative threshold analysis was performed to identify the Lp(a) value below which the misclassification rate (i.e. % of patients with follow-up Lp(a) > 70 mg/dL) remained 70 mg/dL at follow-up compared to 39.9% of those with discharge-Lp(a) >37 mg/dL. Although the median Lp(a) level remained stable between admission and follow-up, one-third of AMI patients shifted within Lp(a) categories over time. Pending external validation, an exploratory two-step strategy based on Lp(a) measurement at discharge, followed by repeat testing in patients with Lp(a) >37 mg/dL, showed a misclassification rate below 1% for identifying patients potentially needing intervention. Clinical trial Number: NCT04050956. This study investigated how lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] levels, a blood protein linked to heart disease risk, change over time following an acute myocardial infarction and identified the optimal timing and testing strategy for Lp(a) measurement. By comparing Lp(a) concentrations at hospital admission, discharge, and follow-up, the study showed that measuring Lp(a) at hospital discharge provides the most reliable assessment of long-term Lp(a) status and future cardiovascular risk.Lp(a) levels can shift meaningfully after a heart attack: Although the average Lp(a) levels remained broadly stable overtime, nearly one in three patients switched to a different risk category between hospital admission and follow-up several months later. This suggests that a single measurement taken at hospital admission for the heart attack may not reliably reflect a patient’s long-term Lp(a) level. A simple two-step measurement strategy can identify patients who may benefit from future specific Lp(a)-lowering treatments: Measuring Lp(a) at hospital discharge was found to be the most reliable approach. Patients with a discharge Lp(a) level at or below 37 mg/dL (approximately three-quarters of patients) could be reassured that they were unlikely to have a high Lp(a) level at follow-up, with fewer than 1 in 100 being incorrectly classified. Only patients with levels above 37 mg/dL at discharge need a second confirmatory measurement before a treatment decision. External validation is required before clinical implementation.
authors: FRENCHIE-Lp(a) Investigators and the French Alliance for Cardiovascular Trials (FACT) investigators network

Thymectomy Extent, Immune Recovery, and Infectious Burden After Neonatal Cardiac Surgery.
items.abstract: Neonatal cardiac surgery frequently requires thymectomy, but the consequences of extensive thymic removal remain uncertain. We retrospectively studied 105 neonates undergoing sternotomy (2015-2024), comparing infections and 6-month lymphocyte recovery after partial versus total thymectomy, with Firth regression adjusted for bypass duration and surgical era. Separate cohorts underwent paired plasma biomarker (n=8) and whole-blood RNA sequencing (n=4) analysis before and after thymectomy. Among 105 neonates, 27 underwent partial and 78 total thymectomy. Multiple infections occurred in 2 of 27 (7%) after partial and 23 of 78 (30%) after total thymectomy (P=0.02); after adjustment for bypass duration and surgical era, the association was not statistically significant (Firth-adjusted odds ratio, 2.99 [95% CI, 0.82-15.85]; P=0.10). Median lymphocyte count decreased after total but increased after partial thymectomy (change, -0.8 versus +0.9×10 3 /μL; P=0.011). Tumor necrosis factor-α decreased in all 8 biomarker participants (unadjusted P=0.0078). RNA sequencing in 4 patients (2 partial, 2 total thymectomy) identified 835 differentially expressed genes; pre-T-cell receptor α decreased in all 4 pairs (log2 fold change, -2.50; adjusted P=6×10 -6 ). Total thymectomy was associated with reduced 6-month lymphocyte recovery and higher unadjusted odds of multiple infections. The infection association was not statistically significant after adjustment, and few events (2 of 27 after partial thymectomy) limit precision and cannot exclude a clinically important effect; these findings are hypothesis-generating. Biomarker and transcriptomic findings are exploratory and cannot distinguish thymectomy from surgery, maturation, or postoperative recovery. Prospective studies are underway to evaluate thymic preservation and autologous reimplantation.

Trends and Frontiers in Stem Cell Research for Sepsis: A Bibliometric Analysis (1990-2025).
items.abstract: To systematically map the 35-year intellectual evolution of stem cell research in sepsis and identify emerging frontiers for clinical translation. We retrieved 3890 publications (1990-2025) from the Web of Science Core Collection. Multi-dimensional bibliometric analyses, including co-citation networks, keyword bursts, and alluvial flow mapping, were performed using CiteSpace, HistCite, and R to delineate the field's trajectory. Annual publications increased significantly, peaking in 2024, with the USA and China as primary contributors. The research focus has undergone a major paradigm shift: from early "bone marrow transplantation" and hematopoietic reconstitution (1990s-2000s) to the immunomodulatory mechanisms of "mesenchymal stem cells" (2010s). Currently, the field has entered a "cell-free" era, characterized by intense research into "extracellular vesicles" and "exosomes" (2021-2025). Alluvial analysis identified "cancer", "immunotherapy", and "COVID-19" as dominant integrated modules. Notably, the emergence of "guidelines" and "precision care" highlights a growing emphasis on clinical standardization and targeted treatment for sepsis-induced organ failure. This study demonstrates that the frontier of sepsis therapy is moving toward refined, secretome-based biologics. Our findings provide a strategic roadmap for researchers to prioritize high-potential therapeutic targets and for clinicians to design more focused trials, ultimately accelerating the integration of stem cell-derived products into mainstream sepsis management.

items.title: Next-Generation Cancer Nanovaccines: Reprogramming the Tumor Microenvironment from Rational Design Toward Clinical Translation.
items.abstract: Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for inducing durable and tumour-specific immune responses; however, their clinical efficacy remains limited by poor antigen immunogenicity, inefficient delivery, tumor heterogeneity, and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in nanotechnology have expanded opportunities for the rational engineering of multifunctional nanoparticle (NP) platforms that can protect therapeutic cargo, enhance antigen presentation and lymphatic transport, co-deliver immunostimulatory adjuvants, and potentially improve immune modulation while reducing systemic exposure. This narrative review provides an overview of next-generation cancer nanovaccines, including lipid-, polymer-, peptide-, inorganic-, biomimetic-, theranostic, in situ-, and stimuli-responsive platforms, with emphasis on their physicochemical design principles, mechanisms of immune activation, and interactions with the TME. Particular attention is given to strategies targeting tumor -associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory T cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and tumor cells to support dendritic-cell maturation, cytotoxic T-cell activation, and anti-tumor immunity. Emerging personalized approaches, including neoantigen- and autologous cell-based nanovaccines, mRNA vaccine platforms, and combinations with immune checkpoint inhibitors, are also discussed. In addition, we examine the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational immunology in neoantigen prioritization, nanoparticle formulation optimization, immunogenicity prediction, and patient-specific vaccine design. Despite encouraging preclinical findings, most cancer nanovaccine platforms remain at the preclinical or early clinical stage, and translation is limited by tumor heterogeneity, variable immune responses, long-term safety and biodistribution concerns, manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory requirements. Overall, the integration of nanotechnology, immunology, precision medicine, and AI offers considerable potential to advance personalized cancer vaccination, but broader clinical validation and standardized manufacturing and evaluation frameworks are required before these platforms can achieve routine clinical application.

items.title: IDO1 Inhibitor RY103 Prevents Sepsis-Associated Immunosuppression in Cecal Ligation and Puncture Mice.
items.abstract: Prolonged immunosuppression is a major risk factor for sepsis death. The mechanism of sepsis-associated immunosuppression remains unclear, hindering timely and targeted immunotherapy. The immunomodulatory enzyme, indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), is overactivated in patients with sepsis; however, its role in sepsis-associated immunosuppression remains unclear. In this study, we defined the time window when cecal ligation puncture (CLP) mice, a gold-standard sepsis model, entered the immunosuppressive state and confirmed elevated IDO1 activity during this phase. The IDO1 inhibitor prevented the occurrence of immunosuppression in CLP mice by decreasing the concentration of interleukin-10 (IL-10), the number of regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and increasing the proportion of M1 macrophages, which led to clearance of pathogenic bacteria in the peritoneal cavity. The IDO1 inhibitor enhanced resistance to infection and improved the survival of septic mice during secondary infection with Staphylococcus aureus . Finally, we explored the potential role of IDO1 in macrophages, key participants in the progression of sepsis. IDO1 preferentially promoted IL-10 production in septic macrophages through the aryl hydrocarbon receptor-STAT3 axis. In macrophages, IDO1 inhibited the mammalian target of rapamycin pathway by depleting ambient tryptophan, leading to the downregulation of the mitochondrial biogenesis regulator peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α) and the metabolic reprogramming mediator hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α). The downregulation of PGC-1α and HIF-1α inhibited mitochondrial biogenesis and glycolysis, respectively, both of which were essential for immune defense. These results demonstrate that IDO1 is a crucial mediator of sepsis-associated immunosuppression, and that targeting IDO1 could serve as a therapeutic strategy for sepsis. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s43657-026-00339-9.

items.title: Real-world treatment patterns in stage IB-IIIC non-small cell lung cancer in China: the KEY-RAISE study.
items.abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths in China. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common type of lung cancer. The treatment landscape for early and locally advanced NSCLC changed considerably between 2019 and 2021. However, there are currently limited data available to inform optimal timing, sequencing, and combinations of different treatment modalities for early-stage NSCLC in China. Therefore, we conducted a real-world study of patients with stage IB-IIIC NSCLC in China to characterize treatment patterns and identify practice gaps. This retrospective, observational study was conducted at 10 sites across China in adults with newly diagnosed stage IB-IIIC NSCLC between January 01, 2019, and December 31, 2021 (identification period). The observation period was from treatment initiation to June 30, 2023. The primary outcomes included descriptions of treatment patterns by initial treatment modalities. Patients (n=1,000) were mostly male (69.6%) with a mean age of 60.4 years, current/former smokers (52.9%), had non-squamous cell carcinoma (64.0%), and clinical stage III disease (54.8%). Among the 281 patients who received epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) testing, including 185 during surgery, EGFR mutations were identified in 174 cases (exon 21 L858R 47.7%; exon 19 deletion 33.3%). Of the 761 patients who underwent surgery (R0 resection 96.2%; lobectomy 83.6%), most received surgery plus systemic therapy (74.0%), primarily adjuvant treatment (79.6%). The rate of non-surgical treatments increased with initial clinical stage. Of the 239 patients not undergoing surgery, 78.2% received systemic therapy alone and 21.8% radiotherapy plus systemic therapy [concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT): 25.5%; sequential chemoradiotherapy (sCRT): 74.5%; immunotherapy consolidation: 26.9%]. Among the 600 patients who underwent surgery plus systemic therapy, 9.7% received neoadjuvant only, 79.7% adjuvant only, and 10.6% perioperative treatment, and the median real-world time on treatment (rwToT) was 2.1, 8.5, and 10.1 months, respectively. This study provides a reference for real-world treatment patterns for stage IB-IIIC NSCLC during the early immunotherapy period of treatment landscape change in China.

items.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptome analyses unveil that MYH11 links stemness to immunotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
items.abstract: Immunotherapy is an essential treatment strategy for lung cancer, yet resistance to it is often unavoidable, resulting in treatment failure and poor prognosis. The cancer stem cell (CSC) theory offers a valuable perspective for understanding tumor metastasis and resistance to immunotherapy. However, there is a scarcity of multi-omics studies that identify tumor stemness subpopulations and their associated signaling pathways. In this study, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics sequencing (ST-seq) to identify a myosin heavy chain 11 ( MYH11) -high stemness subpopulation linked to immunotherapy resistance. We conducted quality control and removed batch effects from two scRNA-seq datasets, then annotated cell types using established marker genes. Malignant cells were distinguished from epithelial cells with fastCNV. Stemness subpopulations were identified using a machine learning-derived messenger RNA (mRNA) stemness index (mRNAsi) and CytoTRACE analysis. To functionally characterize the stemness subpopulation, we employed Monocle3 pseudotime trajectory analysis, CellChat cell-cell communication analysis, and predicted transcription factors (TFs). We also performed consensus clustering on bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data, followed by immune-related scoring, immune cell deconvolution, and drug sensitivity prediction. Clinical validation was achieved through multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Experimental validation included short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated MYH11 knockdown, real-time quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) and western blot analyses, and tumor sphere formation assays to assess cancer stemness. We identified nine major cell types and found a significant enrichment of epithelial cells in tumors resistant to immunotherapy. Using fastCNV, we identified malignant cells and defined seven malignant cell subtypes based on stemness scoring. Notably, the Stem-subtype was significantly enriched in resistant tumors. Functional analysis showed that the Stem-subtype could differentiate into other malignant cell subtypes, with a strong enrichment in the NOTCH signaling pathway. Analysis of fibroblast subpopulations revealed that MYH11 + fibroblasts were closely linked to the Stem-subtype, collectively contributing to immunotherapy resistance. Consensus clustering identified two stemness-related subtypes, with Stemness I associated with poor prognosis. Immune scoring and immune cell analysis further indicated an unfavorable response to immunotherapy in Stemness I. Drug sensitivity prediction identified potential therapeutic agents, and in silico knockout experiments revealed downstream target genes. Validation with clinical samples confirmed that MYH11 -high cancer cells were closely correlated with exhausted CD8 + T cell infiltration and poor immunotherapy outcomes. Experimental validation demonstrated that MYH11 knockdown significantly reduced the expression levels of CXCL12 and TUBA1A , as well as the expression of core NOTCH pathway genes. Furthermore, the tumor sphere-forming capacity was markedly suppressed. In summary, our multi-omics analysis revealed a MYH11 -high malignant cell stemness subpopulation and a MYH11 + fibroblast subpopulation, both of which are closely linked to immunotherapy resistance and poor prognosis in lung cancer.

items.title: Ectasia to Ecstatic: A Case Report of Immunoglobulin G4-Related Disease Masquerading as Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
items.abstract: Immunoglobulin G4-sclerosing cholangitis (IgG4-SC) is a rare fibroinflammatory disease that involves the biliary duct and can often mimic primary sclerosing cholangitis. It is a chronic disease that has the potential to progress to cirrhosis if left untreated. Obtaining a biopsy and serum IgG levels are crucial for diagnosis and understanding the extent of the disease. Here, we present a case of IgG4-SC in a woman with no prior biliary history, who initially presented with mid-abdominal pain and jaundice. She underwent endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, which demonstrated a distal biliary stricture requiring stenting, although imaging demonstrated concern for autoimmune cholangitis given the diffuse ectasia seen. Serum IgG4 levels were found to be four times the upper limit of normal and liver biopsy was consistent with IgG4-related disease, so the patient was started on glucocorticoids with a positive response. IgG4-SC can be a difficult diagnosis to obtain and often mimics other pathologies, so it is an important diagnostic consideration given that it can typically be treated within the correct clinical context.

items.title: Diagnostic challenge of delayed immune-related hepatitis during zongertinib treatment after nivolumab plus ipilimumab in a 52-year-old man with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
items.abstract: Delayed immune-related hepatitis after discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is increasingly recognized, but attribution is difficult when liver injury develops during subsequent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This diagnostic dilemma has not been well described during human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-selective TKI treatment after dual ICI therapy. A 52-year-old Japanese man with HER2 exon 20 insertion-positive stage IVB non-small cell lung cancer received nivolumab plus ipilimumab from February 28 to November 13, 2025, and developed grade 2 oral mucositis, grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, and grade 1-2 skin toxicity. Zongertinib was initiated on November 26. Routine testing on January 6, 2026 showed grade 3 hepatocellular injury, and zongertinib was withheld. Despite drug withdrawal, liver injury progressed, and he was admitted with mild fatigue on January 20, when aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase levels were 774, 1,386, 156, and 160 U/L, respectively. Total bilirubin remained approximately 1.0 mg/dL. Viral and autoimmune testing and imaging disclosed no alternative cause. Liver biopsy showed active hepatitis with lymphocyte-predominant portal and lobular inflammation and interface activity, findings compatible with an immune-mediated hepatitis pattern but not specific for the causative agent. Prednisolone 40 mg/day (approximately 0.5 mg/kg/day) produced rapid biochemical improvement with resolution of fatigue. Zongertinib was resumed on February 11 and continued without recurrent hepatitis through June 2026. The progression of liver injury despite zongertinib withdrawal, multiple prior immune-related adverse events, exclusion of competing causes, compatible histology, corticosteroid responsiveness, and absence of recurrence after zongertinib rechallenge collectively favored delayed immune-related hepatitis, although zongertinib-associated drug-induced liver injury could not be completely excluded. In similar cases, a structured etiological assessment, including liver biopsy when the result may alter cancer treatment, can help guide management.

items.title: Health-care burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in European tertiary-care outpatient clinics (CONSTANS): a prospective multicentre cohort study.
items.abstract: Despite modeling-based epidemiological studies of MASLD, precise estimates of the prevalence and health-care resource utilization in outpatient clinical practice are unknown. We assessed, in a real-life setting, the prevalence of suspected/confirmed MASLD and described health-care resource utilization. A prospective, observational study of patients attending the outpatient hepato-gastroenterology clinics of eight European tertiary care centers during three months. Follow-up data of patients with suspected/confirmed MASLD were recorded 12 months after the screening visit: final diagnosis, disease stage, diagnostic work-up and the use of health-care resources. 5240 outpatients from Germany, France, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Italy, Spain and Slovakia were screened. The main reasons for visit were: chronic viral hepatitis, 33.4% (1749/5240), miscellaneous hepatobiliary conditions including neoplasms, 32.9% (1725/5240) and known/suspected MASLD, 24.7% (1293/5240) (pooled prevalence of 26.1% (95% CI: 19.1-34.7)). 1134 suspected/confirmed MASLD patients were included, the diagnosis was confirmed in 80.2% (909/1134). Significant fibrosis was documented in 22.7% (257/1134) and cirrhosis (including burn-out MASLD) in 21.3% (241/1134). Procedures performed differed between countries, overall 66.4% (753/1134) had imaging studies, 65.3% (740/1134) non-invasive fibrosis tests, 20.4% (231/1134) liver biopsy, while referral for further cardiometabolic assessment or therapy was minimal (144/1134, 15.8%). The cost of all procedures and visits was in the range of that recommended for exploring hepatitis C before treatment, although highly variable between countries. MASLD was the second most frequent single cause for outpatient visits in eight European tertiary care centers. Significant fibrosis including cirrhosis was diagnosed in 44% of patients. The cost of required additional visits and procedures was equivalent to that recommended for hepatitis C before antiviral treatment. IMI2-Grant Agreement 777377-LITMUS.

items.title: Gadoxetic acid in China: a narrative review of the 15-year journey and the road ahead.
items.abstract: Since its pivotal introduction in 2011, gadoxetic acid has fundamentally revolutionized the landscape of hepatobiliary imaging in China, shifting the diagnostic paradigm from morphological assessment toward functional hepatocyte-level evaluation. This review comprehensively summarizes its 15-year clinical evolution within the Chinese healthcare system, exploring its pharmacological benefits, advanced applications, and future integration with data-driven frameworks. A systematic literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, spanning from 2011 to 2026. The search targeted peer-reviewed articles, consensus statements, clinical guidelines, and high-impact reviews published in English and Chinese regarding gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Gadoxetic acid provides high sensitivity for early small hepatocellular carcinoma (sHCC) detection via specific OATP1B3 uptake. Beyond lesion detection, its quantitative mapping shows potential for estimating hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and risk stratification for post-hepatectomy liver failure. Crucially, the ongoing paradigm shift toward integrating radiomics and deep learning bridges macroscopic imaging and microscopic molecular biology, theoretically enabling a multi-dimensional profile of liver parenchyma and lesions within a single diagnostic session. However, a significant gap remains between retrospective predictive performance and clinical readiness, and these data-driven frameworks currently serve as supplementary investigational engines rather than standalone clinical decision-makers. Moving forward, integrating these high-dimensional signatures into constructs such as "digital twin" represents the next frontier. Furthermore, China's hepatitis B virus-dominant epidemiological cohorts, comprehensive multi-modal datasets, "Med-Engineering" fusion, and collaborative networks uniquely accelerate the development and preliminary validation of these models, offering valuable insights for global precision hepatology within China's healthcare system. Over the past 15 years, gadoxetic acid has evolved far beyond a conventional liver imaging tool in China. While clinical translation of advanced analytics requires rigorous, prospective multicenter validation to ensure safety, combining this functional imaging agent with data-driven frameworks represents a promising frontier to eventually optimize future radiology workflows and support personalized precision hepatology.

items.title: Rituximab for immune-mediated diseases with oral mucosal involvement: Mechanisms, evidence, and clinical use.
items.abstract: Persistent oral erosions, pain, xerostomia, and scarring occur in several immune-mediated diseases that involve the oral mucosa. Corticosteroids and conventional immunosuppressants can control activity, but relapse and cumulative toxicity complicate prolonged use. Rituximab (RTX), a chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, consistently depletes circulating B cells and has a more variable effect in tissues. Randomized studies provide the clearest support in pemphigus, particularly when RTX is combined early with a short prednisone course. In severe or refractory mucous membrane pemphigoid, including ocular, laryngeal, and other high-risk disease, evidence comes mainly from observational studies and expert recommendations. The evidence is much less certain for oral lichen planus, primary Sjögren disease, chronic erythema multiforme, and other inflammatory conditions with oral findings; routine RTX treatment is not justified in these settings. Before prescribing RTX, clinicians should confirm the diagnosis and consider hepatitis B status, baseline immunoglobulin levels, vaccination status, infection risk, and the need for follow-up monitoring. In this narrative review, the biology of B cell depletion is considered alongside the evidence for individual diseases, treatment choices, safety, and priorities for further study.

items.title: Investigating the Expression and Function of PPP2R1A in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Omics Analysis with in vitro Validation.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to diagnose early and to treat effectively. Protein Phosphatase 2A Regulatory Subunit Aα ( PPP2R1A ), the scaffolding (Aα) subunit of the PP2A holoenzyme, is altered in several cancer types, but its expression pattern, functional significance, and translational relevance in HCC are incompletely understood. Public transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-LIHC, GTEx, GEO, ICGC-LIHC, HPA, TISCH2) and drug-sensitivity databases were integrated to characterize PPP2R1A expression and its associations with survival, biological pathways, and tumor immune infiltration in HCC. Functional effects of PPP2R1A knockdown were assessed in Huh7 cells by RT-qPCR, CCK-8, Transwell, flow-cytometric cell-cycle, and β-galactosidase assays. PPP2R1A was significantly overexpressed in HCC tissues relative to normal liver and was also elevated across several other cancer types. High PPP2R1A expression was associated with shorter overall and disease-specific survival in Kaplan-Meier analysis, although it was not an independent prognostic factor after multivariate adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.051, p = 0.789). PPP2R1A expression correlated positively with transcriptional programs related to cell cycle, MYC, EGFR, MAPK, and WNT signaling, and negatively with p53 pathway activity. At single-cell and spatial resolution, PPP2R1A was enriched in malignant cells and in tumor regions, and its expression correlated with the abundance of several computationally inferred immune cell populations. PPP2R1A knockdown in Huh7 cells reduced proliferation and invasion, induced G2-phase arrest, and decreased MYC, CDK1, and CCNB1 mRNA expression without inducing senescence. Drug-sensitivity screens suggested candidate agents, such as AT-7519, that warrant further investigation in PPP2R1A -high HCC. PPP2R1A is consistently overexpressed in HCC and contributes to the malignant phenotype at least partly through cell-cycle regulation. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and the potential diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic value of PPP2R1A in HCC requires dedicated prospective and functional validation.

items.title: Outcomes of Patients with Rare Cancers Treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors with and Without Lung and/or Liver Metastases (NCI/SWOG S1609).
items.abstract: Limited prior retrospective data, primarily among patients with lung cancer, liver cancer, and melanoma, has indicated that liver metastases are associated with poorer outcomes with chemotherapy, targeted agents, and checkpoint inhibitor therapy. We used a unique clinical trial resource to evaluate whether liver and/or lung metastases were associated with outcomes among patients with rare tumors treated with combination anti-CTLA-4 (cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4) and anti-PD-1 (programmed cell death protein 1) therapy. The basket trial, SWOG trial S1609 (NCT02834013, DART trial), treated 655 eligible patients without lung or liver primary cancers. Associations with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated with Cox regression models. Associations with clinical benefit rate (confirmed complete and partial response or stable disease for 6 months or longer) and treatment-related adverse events (per CTCAEv5) were evaluated using Fisher exact test. There was no significant difference in rates of grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events across the groups. Participants with liver metastases, with or without lung metastases, had a lower likelihood of experiencing clinical benefit (11% and 18%, respectively) compared with participants with lung but not liver metastases or participants with neither lung nor liver metastases (26% and 30%, respectively, p = 0.003). On multivariable analysis, having both lung and liver metastases was associated with shorter PFS and OS compared with the presence of neither liver nor lung metastases when accounting for the number of RECIST (Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors) target sites. Compared with the presence of neither liver nor lung metastases, lung but not liver or liver but not lung sites of metastases were significantly associated with PFS but not OS in these multivariable models. In a diverse cohort of participants with advanced rare tumors treated with combination anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-1 therapy, we found that both the combination of lung and liver metastases was associated with shorter PFS and OS.
items.journal: Journal of immunotherapy and precision oncology

items.title: Segmental distribution of hepatic steatosis on opportunistic low-dose computed tomography: a Couinaud-based analysis.
items.abstract: Hepatic steatosis is commonly and incidentally detected on nonenhanced computed tomography (CT) as areas of low attenuation. Hepatic steatosis is recognized as an independent predictor of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM), underscoring the clinical significance of its detection and characterization. Low-dose CT (LDCT) performed for lung cancer screening offers a unique opportunity for opportunistic evaluation of hepatic steatosis. The objective of this study is to measure CT attenuation across all eight Couinaud liver segments in patients with incidentally detected hepatic steatosis on lung cancer screening LDCT, and to identify clinical correlates of steatosis. This retrospective, single-center study evaluated hepatic steatosis among patients who underwent LDCT for lung cancer screening between 2019 and 2024; patients with steatosis and available 1.5 mm soft-tissue reconstructions comprised the analytic cohort for segmental analysis. Steatosis was defined as mean liver attenuation <40 Hounsfield units (HU) on unenhanced CT. Mean CT attenuation (HU) was measured in each Couinaud segment on soft-tissue 1.5 mm unenhanced reconstructions and normalized to intrathoracic tracheal air to reduce interscan variability related to scanner calibration and acquisition parameters. Segmental differences were assessed by repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey-Kramer post-hoc correction. Associations between mean liver HU and clinical variables [age, gender, coronary artery calcification (CAC) score, body mass index, DM] were evaluated using t-tests, and multivariable linear regression. Among 1,000 patients, steatosis was identified in 79 (7.9%); 68 with available 1.5 mm reconstructions (70.6% male) comprised the analytic cohort. Patients with steatosis were younger (median 61 vs. 63 years, P=0.005) and had higher BMI (mean 32.43 vs. 28.59 kg/m 2 , P=0.01). Mean liver attenuation was -30.9±30.5 HU (range, -109.2 to +27.6 HU). Segmental attenuation ranged from -27.1±30.8 HU in segment 1 (caudate lobe) to -34.0±30.9 HU in segment 7. Repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant segmental variation (P<0.001); segment 1 showed higher attenuation than segments 3, 4A, 4B, 6, 7, and 8 (all Tukey-adjusted P<0.05), indicating relative caudate sparing. Segments 7 and 8 had the lowest attenuation. Within-patient variability was modest (mean standard deviation: 4.91±1.94 HU), though a subset showed substantial heterogeneity. In multivariable linear regression, older age (β=+0.16/year, P=0.001) and female sex (β=+1.51, P=0.03) were independently associated with higher liver attenuation, while DM was associated with lower attenuation (β=-2.44, P=0.001). In this exploratory, single-center study, the mean attenuation of segments 7 and 8 combined correlated strongly with whole-liver attenuation and may represent a practical candidate proxy for opportunistic screening. Validation in a larger study is needed before this two-segment measurement approach is adopted for routine use.
